facts.text: Normandy Park was officially incorporated on June 8, 1953, after the Seattle‑Tacoma Land Company began developing the area in the 1920s.
The city’s first grand clubhouse, built on “Lot A,” hosted free refreshments and band concerts to attract Seattle’s wealthy residents.
During the Great Depression, the Seattle‑Tacoma Land Company abandoned its plans, halting development until the post‑war boom revived the community.
Normandy Park’s historic Russell Waterfall, named after an early pioneer, remains a cherished natural landmark for locals.
The Fort Nisqually Living History Museum, located in Normandy Park, showcases the first European settlement on Puget Sound through costumed interpreters.
The Marine View Park, one of the town’s oldest public spaces, offers sweeping views of Puget Sound and a glimpse into early 20th‑century leisure culture.
